detail.readme:
# skills The CLI for the open agent skills ecosystem. Agent skills are reusable instructions that teach coding agents how to perform tasks, from reviewing code to working with a library. Discover skills at [skills.sh](https://skills.sh). Supports **OpenCode**, **Claude Code**, **Codex**, **Cursor**, and [75 more](docs/agents.md).

## Install a Skill Requires Node.js 22.20 or later. Run this from your project: ```bash npx skills add vercel-labs/agent-skills ``` Choose the skills and coding agents to install to. Skills are installed to the current project by default; add `-g` to make them available across projects. ```bash # Choose one skill and agent npx skills add vercel-labs/agent-skills --skill web-design-guidelines -a claude-code # Browse available skills npx skills find ``` See the [installation reference](docs/commands.md#skills-add) for source formats, private repositories, and all options. ## Other Commands | Command | Description | | --------------------------------- | -------------------------------- | | `npx skills find [query]` | Search for skills | | `npx skills list` | List installed skills | | `npx skills use @` | Use one skill without installing | | `npx skills check` | Check for available updates | | `npx skills update [skills...]` | Update installed skills | | `npx skills remove [skills...]` | Remove installed skills | | `npx skills init [name]` | Create a skill template | Read the [CLI reference](docs/commands.md) or run `npx skills --help` for examples and options. Experimental commands are listed [below](#experimental-features). ## Use a Skill Without Installing Generate a prompt for a skill, or launch a supported coding agent with it: ```bash npx skills use vercel-labs/agent-skills@web-design-guidelines --agent claude-code ``` Omit `--agent` to print the prompt instead. See [`skills use`](docs/commands.md#skills-use). ## Experimental Features
Commands prefixed with experimental_ are previews. Their names, options, and behavior may change or be removed in any release without notice. | Command | Description | | --------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------- | | `npx skills experimental_sync` | Sync skills shipped by npm dependencies into your project | | `npx skills experimental_install` | Restore project skills recorded in `skills-lock.json` | Some npm packages bundle instructions for your agent alongside their code. Sync links them into your project so they update with the dependency, and also installs skill packs declared in `package.json`: ```bash npm install -D skills agent-browser npx skills experimental_sync -y ``` See the [experimental commands reference](docs/commands.md#experimental-commands) for options, the `skills` field, and the [RFC](https://github.com/vercel-labs/skills/issues/2323) behind it.
## Lock File Content Hash `skills-lock.json` (version 2) records a `computedHash` for each project skill. The hash covers the files the CLI installs into `.agents/skills/`, so `list`, `check`, and `install --frozen-lockfile` can compare it with what is on disk. Tools that check skills themselves can compute the same value: 1. Collect every file in the skill folder. Leave out `metadata.json` files and the `.git`, `__pycache__`, and `__pypackages__` folders, because the installer does not copy them. A symlink counts as the file or folder it points to. Leave out a symlink that is broken, loops, or points outside the skill folder. 2. Give each file a path relative to the skill folder, with `/` as the separator. 3. For a text file (a file that contains no NUL byte), replace each CRLF with LF. Do not change binary files. 4. Sort the files by the UTF-8 bytes of their paths. Do not use a locale-aware sort. 5. For each file in that order, feed `path`, a NUL byte, the content length in bytes as decimal ASCII, a NUL byte, and the content into one SHA-256. The content length is counted after step 3. 6. The hash is the lowercase hex digest. Test vectors: | Files | `computedHash` | | -------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------ | | none | `e3b0c44298fc1c149afbf4c8996fb92427ae41e4649b934ca495991b7852b855` | | `SKILL.md` = `# hi\n` | `93c36952d8843b33e68ae970ebabcc03e1687c9bb0dd1ecaf357060318952f55` | | `SKILL.md` = `a\n`, `docs/b.md` = `b\n` | `b22c4d22aa319d2924312fa18fcbfedc88fa89c74dbd8f298c683e1caf7b7f24` | The last vector equals `printf 'SKILL.md\0002\000a\ndocs/b.md\0002\000b\n' | sha256sum`. A version 1 lock is upgraded when it is read, without network access. An installed skill whose files still match its version 1 hash gets a new hash computed from those files. Any other entry gets an empty hash, because there is nothing trusted to check it against. `skills install` fetches those skills again and records new hashes, and `--frozen-lockfile` fails until that is done. ## Supported Agents The CLI detects installed agents and lets you choose where skills are installed. See [all supported agents, installation paths, and compatibility](docs/agents.md). ## Creating Skills ```bash npx skills init my-skill ``` Edit the generated `SKILL.md` with instructions for your agent. See [creating and sharing skills](docs/creating-skills.md) for the format and discovery rules. ## Documentation - [CLI reference](docs/commands.md): installation, command examples, and experimental features - [Supported agents](docs/agents.md): agent names, skill directories, and compatibility - [Creating skills](docs/creating-skills.md): frontmatter, repository layouts, and plugins - [Troubleshooting and configuration](docs/troubleshooting.md): common problems, environment variables, and telemetry - [Programmatic API](docs/api.md): install and manage skills from your own tools with `import { installSkills } from 'skills'` ## Telemetry The CLI collects anonymous usage data. Set `DISABLE_TELEMETRY=1` or `DO_NOT_TRACK=1` to disable telemetry and security-audit requests. See [what is collected](docs/troubleshooting.md#telemetry). ## Related Links - [Skills Directory](https://skills.sh) - [Agent Skills Specification](https://agentskills.io) - [Vercel Agent Skills](https://github.com/vercel-labs/agent-skills) ## License This project is licensed under the [MIT License](LICENSE).
